title: Active Optical Frequency Measurements with Superradiance Prolonged by a Modulated Magnetic Field
authors: Huihui Yu, Shi-Lei Su, Chongxin Shan, Klaus Mølmer, Yuan Zhang
abstract: Superradiant emission from long-lived excited states of an atomic ensemble confined in an optical cavity constitutes a practical source of light with narrow linewidth. In the pulsed regime, however, superradiance implies rapid emission and a broadening of the spectrum. Recent experiments have demonstrated constructive and destructive interference of superradiant emission by different strontium atomic transitions. In this article, we show that by modulating the atomic transition frequencies with a magnetic field, it is possible to control the release of the atomic excitation energy as a prolonged pulse or a train of superradiant pulses. By simulations, we show that heterodyne detection of the prolonged superradiance shows extremely sharp spectral features, which leads to significantly reduced frequency uncertainty and fluctuation.
summary: The paper demonstrates how modulating an external magnetic field can actively control superradiant emission from an atom-cavity system, transforming rapid pulses into sustained or periodic trains. This engineered coherence leads to dramatically narrower spectral features when measured via heterodyne detection. The result shows a significant enhancement in the precision of optical frequency measurements.
main_problem: The goal is to actively control the release of superradiant excitation energy, which is normally rapid and spectrally broad, by modulating atomic transition frequencies using a magnetic field.
main_result: Modulating the magnetic field allows for the prolongation of superradiant pulses or generating pulse trains, leading to significantly sharper spectral features and substantially reduced frequency uncertainty in heterodyne detection.
method: The study uses theoretical modeling based on the stochastic master equation solved via cumulant mean-field approaches, supplemented by numerical simulations.
model_or_system: The system involves superradiant emission from a long-lived excited state of an atomic ensemble (Sr-87) confined within an optical cavity. The dynamics are controlled by applying time-dependent magnetic fields that induce Zeeman shifts on the atomic transitions.
key_observables: Superradiant emission intensity, intra-cavity photon number, Bloch vectors ($\mathbf{A}_{9/2}, \mathbf{A}_{-9/2}$), and frequency uncertainty quantified via Fractional Frequency Difference (FFD).
important_parameters: Cavity frequency ($\omega_c$), damping rate ($\kappa$), coupling strength ($g$), and the time-dependent magnetic field modulation $\mathbf{B}(t)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on stochastic master equations solved using cumulant mean-field approximations, which are necessary to incorporate measurement backaction from heterodyne detection.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate system schematics, Bloch vector rotations under magnetic control, and power spectra comparing short vs. prolonged superradiance pulses, demonstrating linewidth narrowing.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework using stochastic master equations, details the application of cumulant mean-field approximations for heterodyne detection, simulates the effect of time-dependent magnetic fields to engineer pulse trains, and quantifies the resulting improvement in frequency measurement precision.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum control in cavity QED systems by using external fields (magnetic) to manipulate collective atomic emission dynamics, which is a core topic in AMO physics and quantum optics.
